ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Make sure they can reach food: meals in stock, a food policy that allows what you have, and food inside their allowed area. A cook at work keeps meals coming. It goes as soon as they eat.
Give them enough sleep hours in the Schedule tab, and a bed close to where they work so the night isn't spent walking. It goes once they've slept.
Give them recreation hours in the Schedule tab and several kinds of recreation to choose from, such as horseshoes, a chess table or an instrument. The same kind over and over stops satisfying them.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Give them free time and recreation
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep several kinds of recreation, and some free time in every day.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Clean away blood, dirt and debris where they spend their time, and add art, flowers, plants and nicer floors.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Clean up and add some art
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep the places they use clean and pretty: art, plants and good floors.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Give them comfortable places to sit and sleep: chairs or armchairs at tables and workbenches, and better beds. Better quality furniture is more comfortable.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Give them good chairs and beds
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Comfortable chairs and beds keep this up.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Give them time under the open sky: outdoor work such as growing, hauling or hunting, or recreation outside. Long stretches indoors, and under a mountain most of all, wear on them.
This colonist prefers a roof over their head: give them indoor work and keep them out of the open where you can.
Make the rooms where they spend their time bigger, or take out furniture that crowds them.
Children need to learn and play: give them lessons, a school desk or blackboard, toys and someone to play with.
Light the places where they work and walk after dark: torches, braziers or lamps.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Light where they work and walk

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Heat or cool the rooms they use: a campfire or heater in the cold, a passive cooler or a cooler in the heat. Clothes suited to the season widen the range they're comfortable in.
Rotting corpses give off a stink that hangs in the air. Haul them away and bury or burn them well clear of where people live and work; the air clears soon after.
Give the fallen a resting place: dig a grave or build a sarcophagus, and have someone carry them there. Cremating them ends it too.
Haul corpses out of sight, into graves or a dumping zone away from paths and rooms. The memory fades on its own.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Haul the corpses out of sight

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Roof over the paths they use most, and avoid outdoor work in heavy rain. It passes once they dry off.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Keep them out of the rain

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A condition across the whole map is weighing on them: a psychic drone, toxic fallout, a noxious haze. It ends when that does. Until then, good meals, recreation and rest make up for it.
Make the room more impressive: more space, cleaner, better furniture and some art.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep the room clean and well furnished.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Improve their bedroom: more space, cleaner, better bed and furniture, some art.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep their bedroom clean. The bonus comes back every night they sleep there.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Give them a bedroom of their own. Even a small private room beats a shared barracks.
Give them a bed under a roof, even a simple one.
Keep bedrooms at a comfortable temperature: a heater or campfire nearby in winter, a passive cooler in summer.
Give them a bedroom of their own, and keep busy paths, doors and noisy work away from where people sleep.
Give each colonist their own bed. Only lovers and spouses want to share.
Assign the couple to one double bed in a room of their own.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Give the couple a double bed

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Greedy colonists want an impressive bedroom of their own. Give them the best one, or improve theirs.
Jealous colonists want a bedroom at least as good as anyone else's. Even out the bedrooms, or give them the best.
Night owls want to be awake at night: set their schedule to sleep during the day.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep their schedule on nights.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Build a table with chairs near where they eat: a dining room close to the kitchen and food storage.
Give them cooked meals: a cook at a campfire or stove, raw food left off their food policy, and the nutrient paste dispenser kept for hard times.
Store food in a freezer or a cold room, and keep rotten food out of the stockpiles so it doesn't get eaten.
Check their food policy and the cook's bills: leave out corpses, human meat or insect meat for those who mind.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep a good cook making fine or lavish meals.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Make the dining room more impressive: bigger, cleaner, better tables and chairs, art.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep the dining room clean. The bonus applies to every meal eaten there.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Make the recreation room more impressive: more space, cleaner, better furniture, art.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep the recreation room clean and well furnished.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Replace worn clothes: set their apparel policy to drop anything below half condition, and keep a tailor at work.
Set apparel policies to refuse clothes taken from the dead, then burn or sell those clothes.
Take off clothes made of human leather, unless their beliefs welcome them.
Give them clothes: check their apparel policy, and make sure there's something in store for them to wear.
Treat their wounds and let them rest in a medical bed. Healing takes the pain away; some drugs dull it.
Tend the illness with medicine, and let them rest in a clean, well-lit hospital.
This comes from their health: see the Health tab. Treating or curing the condition ends the mood.
Their body wants a drug it depends on. Allow some in their drug policy; for an addiction, sitting out the withdrawal also ends it.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Allow some, or wait it out

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: An operation on them went wrong. The memory fades. Next time, let your best doctor operate, with good medicine, in a clean, well-lit room.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Use the best doctor next time

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Grief takes time. A proper grave or funeral helps, and good moments in between. The days of mourning decree, on the Decrees page, makes it fade faster.
The colony's harsh deeds weigh on them. Do fewer of them, or leave such jobs to those who don't mind. It fades.
Keep bonded animals in the colony: selling or releasing them hurts their person. It fades.
Keep the two apart for a while: different rooms, work and schedules. It fades.
Heartbreak fades with time. Keeping the two apart for a while helps.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Keep the two apart a while

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Parties, weddings and time with loved ones come on their own when people are content. A good room to gather in, and a double bed for each couple, help them along.
The fresh-start glow wears off soon. Get beds, a dining table and recreation in place before it does.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Their child is unhappy or unwell. Look after the child's mood and health, and theirs will follow.
Feed and soothe the baby, and give babies a nursery away from the bedrooms.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Low expectations make them easy to please while the colony is poor. This bonus shrinks as the colony grows richer.
They love this work. Keep it high on their work priorities.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Their title demands a better bedroom. Hover over the mood to see which requirements are missing.
Their title demands a proper throne room. Hover over the mood to see which requirements are missing.
Their title demands certain clothes and meals. Hover over their title in the Character tab to see everything it asks for.
A noble made a demand. Fulfill it while there's time; the letter that announced it says what they want.
This comes from their ideoligion. Honor the belief, or change it when the ideoligion is next reformed.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Their beliefs approve. Keep honoring them.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Their ideoligion wants something in place: the building it asks for, a role filled, or the role's clothes worn.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Give their ideoligion what it asks

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Move gibbet cages and skullspikes away from where they walk, unless their beliefs welcome them.
Their genes want violence: let them hunt or fight in melee now and then.
Let them deathrest in a deathrest casket.
They dislike a decree in force. Repeal it on the Decrees page, or wait for it to run out. Declaring the same decree again soon after makes it sting more each time.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: It lasts while the decree is in force.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Strain drains with quiet nights in a warm bed, free time, parties, long talks with friends and days without fighting. The Heart section of their Mood tab says what built it. The days of rest decree makes it drain about twice as fast.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Give them rest and free time

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: It fades in a day or two. The day they took to themselves also took about 40 points of strain off.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Trust grows when the council listens: grant or promise their wishes, heed their petitions, answer dilemmas the way they would.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep listening to their wishes and petitions.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Their nature clashes with what the colony is known for. Lean the other way in dilemmas and decrees, or give them other reasons to be happy.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Lean the other way in decisions
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: The colony's ways suit them.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Their wish is waiting on the Wishes page. Grant it or promise it before it runs out.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Grant more of what they ask for. A promise kept earns more trust than a wish granted without one.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: This comes from their friends, rivals or mentors; see their bonds. Keep rivals apart and friends together.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keep friends working and eating together.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Secrets fade with time. A vendetta ends when the score is settled, or when it's laid down.
Only a dream. It fades within a day.
A moment with a stranger, a nemesis or an animal. It fades on its own. A nemesis taken prisoner or killed won't come back to frighten them again.
They didn't like how the council answered a dilemma. It fades on its own; answering the next one the way they would helps.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Answer the next one their way
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: They approved of the council's decision.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: This is about their life goal. Help them toward it, or let it go in its own time.
One of their quirks. It comes and goes with what they're doing.
This is about their keepsake. Keep it safe, or return it if it was lost.
Dubs Bad Hygiene: build toilets and something to wash at (a water tub, bath or shower), keep water flowing, and give them time to wash.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Build toilets and somewhere to wash

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A promised wish ran out unanswered. It fades; from now on, promise only what the colony can grant in time. A promise broken hurts more than a wish ignored.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Promise only what you can grant

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: They've watched one colonist get a second wish granted while their own still waits. Grant theirs next, and spread granted wishes more evenly.
They spoke up and weren't heard: an objection overruled, or a request refused. Next time, weigh their objection, or grant something they've asked for.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Being heard at the council matters to them.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Losing a seat stings, and it fades. A wish granted in the meantime softens it, and they can stand again at the next election.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Grant a wish to soften it
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: A seat on the council is an honor. Keep them in it while they do the job well.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: They argued over a decree. It fades on its own; repealing the decree on the Decrees page ends the quarrel.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: The council declared what they asked for.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: The colony missed its ambition. It fades on its own; pick the next one on the Ambition page with time enough to reach it.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: The colony reached its ambition together. Set the next one.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A tradition was broken. Keep it next time, since people expect it now.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Keeping the colony's traditions matters to them.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A name they're not proud of, or one they lost. It fades; deeds earn better names.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: They earned a name and they wear it proudly.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A farewell weighs on them. It fades; time with their other friends helps.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: A proper farewell helps them grieve.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Their keepsake is gone. If it can be found or bought back, that would mean a great deal; otherwise it fades.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Find or buy back the keepsake

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: One of their quirks. It comes and goes with the weather, the dark or what they're doing.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: One of their quirks, and a happy one.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A moment with the council or the colony. It fades; listening to their wishes and petitions keeps trust high.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: A good moment with the council or the colony. These add up.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: An event out in the world. It fades on its own; a good evening, a fine meal or time with friends helps in the meantime.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: A happy event out in the world. It fades on its own.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: The council turned away, or gave up, someone they cared about. It fades with time; granting one of their wishes helps their trust recover.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Grant a wish to ease it

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Their partner's ex lives here now. Keep the two apart at work and at meals, and give it time.
Grief for the home they came from. Nothing to fix; friends, recreation and a good room help them carry it.
Caught out in the hail. It passes within half a day. Roofed walkways keep people out of the next one.
They read the comet as a bad omen. It lasts until the comet fades; nothing else will convince them.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: They read the comet as a good omen, or just think it's beautiful. Stargazing is better while it lasts.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: The colony paid tribute, and it stings for a few days. Stronger defenses make the next demand easier to refuse.

Something the council granted them was taken away and not put back in time; the Why line says what. Put it back within five days and the council makes it right: the mood ends and half the lost trust comes back. A thing being moved or rebuilt still counts as there.
